# 15 Animate class diagrams with the timeline block

## Outcome

A `timeline:` block in a `classDiagram` document reveals and highlights classes and relationships
exactly as it does flowchart nodes and edges — the same four verbs, the same effects, the same
`AnimationController`. This is what makes a class diagram a Siren document rather than a static
picture, and it is the product's stated differentiator (ADR-0001).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `parseClassDiagram` accepts a `timeline:` block with the same syntax the flowchart parser
  accepts, producing the same `SirenTimeline` shape (reuse the existing parsing rather than
  writing a second grammar — extract it if that is what sharing takes, and say so).
- [ ] `buildClassModel` resolves timeline entries against class ids, relationship ids, namespace
  ids and note ids; an unknown id is an error diagnostic and the entry is dropped.
- [ ] `renderClassDiagramToSVG` gives an element with an `enter` action the initial
  `siren-pending` class, and no other element — the same rule `renderToSVG` applies.
- [ ] `render()` returns a controller whose `totalSteps` is the highest declared step, and
  `next()` / `prev()` / `reset()` move classes and relationships through the same class
  transitions as a flowchart's nodes and edges.
- [ ] An `exit` on a class whose relationships remain visible produces the same advisory warning
  `buildFlowchartModel` gives for an edge outliving its endpoint — or, if that warning is
  genuinely flowchart-specific, say why it does not apply and do not fake it.
- [ ] A class diagram with no `timeline:` block still renders everything immediately visible, with
  `totalSteps === 0`.


- [ ] Any `siren-*` class you newly emit has a matching rule in `theme/default.css`. The coverage
  test in `theme/default.test.ts` (added by ticket 16, which now runs before this one) fails
  otherwise — that guard exists precisely so a new class cannot ship unthemed, which is how the
  sequence board shipped an invisible diagram.

## Test seam

`parseClassDiagram` (unit), `buildClassModel` (unit), `renderClassDiagramToSVG` (jsdom), and
`render()` + `controller.next()` (integration, jsdom) — the animation behavior is only really
proven at the last one.

This ticket is cross-cutting by nature: it is one behavior that necessarily spans all four
pipeline files. It runs alone rather than being split into four tickets that each deliver nothing
observable.
